name: Fv
description: The minimal antigen-binding unit: a VH–VL heterodimer with no constant domains.

name: scFv
description: VH and VL carried on one polypeptide and held together by a flexible linker.

name: Fab
description: Heavy-chain Fd (VH–CH1) disulfide-bonded to a complete light chain.

name: F(ab')2
description: Two Fab arms held together by the hinge disulfides, with no Fc.

name: VHH (nanobody)
description: A single camelid heavy-chain variable domain that binds without a light chain.

name: Biparatopic VHH
description: Two VHH domains in tandem, each raised against a different epitope on one target.

name: Trivalent VHH
description: Three linked VHH domains giving three binding specificities on one short chain.

name: IgG1
description: The parental monospecific, bivalent antibody that every format below modifies.

name: Fc
description: The hinge–CH2–CH3 homodimer on its own, the effector and half-life module.

name: One-armed IgG
description: Monovalent IgG: one Fab arm, a bare knob-into-hole Fc on the other side.

name: Knob-into-hole
description: Reciprocal CH3 steric mutations drive heterodimerisation of two different heavy chains.

name: Common light chain
description: Both arms share one light chain, so only heavy-chain pairing has to be engineered. The shared chain carries both specificities, per the AbML convention.

name: CrossMab CH1-CL
description: CH1 and CL are exchanged in one arm, so the wrong light chain can no longer pair.

name: CrossMab VH-VL
description: VH and VL are exchanged in one arm, keeping the constant-domain interface untouched.

name: CrossMab Fab
description: The whole Fab is swapped in one arm — both the variable and the constant pair cross over.

name: Orthogonal Fab
description: Complementary charge and steric mutations across both Fab interfaces enforce correct pairing.

name: Charge-pair bispecific
description: Electrostatic steering: opposing charges at the CH3 and CH1/CL interfaces instead of knobs.

name: DuetMab
description: Knob-into-hole plus an engineered CH1–CL disulfide replacing the native one in one arm.

name: kappa-lambda body
description: One common heavy chain pairs with a kappa and a lambda light chain, giving two specificities.

name: DVD-Ig
description: A second variable domain stacked N-terminal to each native one: tetravalent and bispecific.

name: IgG-scFv (heavy C-term)
description: An scFv fused to each heavy-chain C-terminus — tetravalent, bispecific, symmetric.

name: IgG-scFv (light C-term)
description: The same idea with the scFv hung off each light-chain C-terminus instead.

name: scFv-IgG (heavy N-term)
description: An scFv placed ahead of each VH, so the second specificity sits at the tip of the arm.

name: IgG-VHH
description: A single VHH domain on each heavy-chain C-terminus — the smallest symmetric append.

name: Two-in-one Fab (DAF)
description: One paratope engineered to bind two antigens, so the molecule stays a plain IgG.

name: ADC (site-specific)
description: An IgG carrying defined conjugation sites for a cytotoxic payload.

name: BiTE (tandem scFv)
description: Two scFvs in tandem on one chain — the T-cell engager archetype, no Fc at all.

name: Diabody
description: A 5-residue linker is too short for VH to fold back onto its own VL, so two chains cross-pair.

name: scDiabody
description: The diabody folded onto a single chain by adding a third, longer middle linker.

name: DART
description: A diabody locked by an added C-terminal interchain disulfide for stability.

name: TandAb
description: Two identical four-domain chains dimerise head-to-tail into a tetravalent bispecific.

name: Triplebody
description: Three scFvs in a row on one chain, giving three specificities without an Fc.

name: scFv-Fc
description: An scFv on each side of an Fc: bivalent, monospecific, roughly half the mass of an IgG.

name: VHH-Fc (HCAb)
description: Camelid-style heavy-chain-only antibody: one VHH per chain, straight onto the hinge.

name: Bispecific VHH-Fc
description: Two different VHH domains on a knob-into-hole Fc — the compact asymmetric bispecific.

name: Tandem scFv-Fc
description: Two tandem scFvs per chain on an Fc: tetravalent and bispecific, fully symmetric.

name: Diabody-Fc
description: A diabody grafted onto an Fc, which restores long serum half-life.

name: Receptor-Fc trap
description: A soluble receptor ectodomain on an Fc, used to soak up a ligand.

name: Zipper-assembled bispecific
description: A leucine zipper on each C-terminus forces the two different half-antibodies together.

name: Trispecific IgG-scFv
description: A knob-into-hole bispecific with a third specificity appended as an scFv on one chain.

name: Trispecific VHH-Fc
description: Three VHH domains distributed across a knob-into-hole Fc.

name: 2+1 TCB (CrossMab CH1-CL)
description: Bivalent for the tumour antigen, monovalent for CD3. The tumour Fab is fused head-to-tail to the N-terminus of the CD3 CrossFab, which sits proximal to the hinge. Cibisatamab geometry.

name: 2+1 TCB (CrossMab VH-VL, charged)
description: The same 2:1 geometry with VH/VL exchanged in the CD3 Fab instead, plus charge pairs in the untouched Fabs to suppress the Bence-Jones-like side product. Glofitamab geometry.

name: TCR alpha-beta
description: The alpha/beta T-cell receptor ectodomain pair.

name: TCR gamma-delta
description: The gamma/delta T-cell receptor ectodomain pair.
